claim: Resolution with unification is sound and refutation complete; a saturation prover must be fair or completeness is lost, and a run ends in one of three ways: empty clause, saturation (satisfiable), or non-termination.
agent_test: Give the agent a 3-way outcome check (proved, closed/saturated, budget out) and compare to an agent that only has success/timeout.

claim: Default clause selection interleaves an age queue and a weight queue at a fixed ratio; mixing a blind (oldest-first) pick with a greedy (lightest) pick is the standard hedge. Indirect LLM support: pure best-first without a fairness mechanism collapsed on hard instances (d05).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare pure best-first step choice with a 1:k mix of oldest-open and most-promising-open items.

claim: Adding more layered clause-selection queues keyed on cheap features (theory content, goal distance, Horn closeness) raises solved counts; the union of heuristics gains far more than any one (TPTP +1,189 over base).
agent_test: Run several cheap selection rules in rotation and measure union coverage vs the best single rule at equal tokens.

claim: Learned clause guidance helps most when mixed into the prover's own queues, and fails as a full replacement: net-only queue solved 25% of baseline, layered mix 136-137% (Vampire/SMT-LIB).
agent_test: Compare learned step-scorer alone, default alone, and a 1:1 / 1:2 layered mix at equal tokens.

claim: Pure neural guidance in E on Mizar without a switch to fast heuristics proved fewer hard theorems than unguided E (137 vs 145; 383 vs 458) because the network is slow; a two-phase switch gave 4.34% vs 2.33%.
agent_test: Charge scorer cost in tokens; test a costly-then-cheap two-phase schedule vs one-phase at equal tokens.
